  apply Lp.ext
  have hcoe := hf.coeFn_toLp

    (Measure.measurePreserving_neg (volume : Measure ℝ)).quasiMeasurePreserving.tendsto_ae
  filter_upwards [l2Reflection_ae (hf.toLp f), hneg, hcoe] with x href hleft hright
  have hleft' : ((hf.toLp f : SoninL2) : ℝ → ℂ) (-x) = f (-x) := by
    simpa [Function.comp_apply] using hleft
  rw [href, hleft', hright, heven]

  ⟨(memLp_two_burnolCoPoissonRightSum_coPoissonIndicatorSeed hb hb1).toLp _,

  (memLp_two_burnolCoPoissonRightSum_coPoissonIndicatorSeed hb hb1).coeFn_toLp

/-- **The aperture head of the indicator co-Poisson vector is constant.**  This is the first of the
two defining Sonine conditions. -/
theorem soninHeadConstant_coPoissonIndicatorEven {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b ≤ 1) :
    SoninHeadConstant b (((coPoissonIndicatorEven hb hb1 : evenSubspace) : SoninL2) : ℝ → ℂ) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := soninHeadConstant_burnolCoPoissonRightSum (support_coPoissonIndicatorSeed b)
  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae (coPoissonIndicatorEven_coeFn hb hb1), hc] with t h1 h2
  rw [h1, h2]

/-- **The co-Poisson layer is inhabited as soon as the cosine head condition holds.**  Every other
field of a co-Poisson source is supplied unconditionally by the indicator seed: integrability,
compact multiplicative support, square integrability, evenness, constancy of the aperture head, and
the almost-everywhere identification of the vector with the literal co-Poisson sum. -/
def coPoissonIndicatorSource {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b ≤ 1)

      (((soninCosineUnitary (coPoissonIndicatorEven hb hb1) : evenSubspace) : SoninL2) : ℝ → ℂ)) :
    BurnolCoPoissonSource b where
  seed := coPoissonIndicatorSeed b
  seed_integrable := integrable_coPoissonIndicatorSeed b
  seed_support := support_coPoissonIndicatorSeed b
  vector := ⟨coPoissonIndicatorEven hb hb1,
    mem_soninExtendedSpace.mpr ⟨soninHeadConstant_coPoissonIndicatorEven hb hb1, hcos⟩⟩
  vector_eq_sum := coPoissonIndicatorEven_coeFn hb hb1

theorem nonempty_burnolCoPoissonSource_of_cosineHead {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b ≤ 1)

    Nonempty (BurnolCoPoissonSource b) :=
  ⟨coPoissonIndicatorSource hb hb1 hcos⟩

intertwining says that the cosine transform of a co-Poisson sum is the co-Poisson sum of the
reciprocal seed.  Granting that identity for the indicator seed, the second Sonine condition follows
from the first one applied to the reciprocal seed, which is again supported in the window. -/
theorem soninHeadConstant_cosine_coPoissonIndicatorEven_of_intertwine

        SoninL2)) : ℝ → ℂ) =ᵐ[volume]
      burnolCoPoissonRightSum (coPoissonReciprocalSeed (coPoissonIndicatorSeed b))) :
    SoninHeadConstant b
      (((soninCosineUnitary (coPoissonIndicatorEven hb hb1) : evenSubspace) : SoninL2) :
        ℝ → ℂ) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := soninHeadConstant_burnolCoPoissonRightSum
    (support_coPoissonReciprocalSeed hb (support_coPoissonIndicatorSeed b))
  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae hint, hc] with t h1 h2
  rw [h1, h2]

This module assembles a completed Xi-divisor comparison target in degrees zero, one, and two:

* `H^0 = C`;
* `H^1 = ell^2` completion of the source jet associated graded;
* `H^2 = C(-1)`.

The endpoint cup pairing is multiplication followed by the degree-two trace.  The middle cup is
the completed oriented alternating form.  Both Poincare pairings are nondegenerate, cup followed
by Hodge star is positive, endpoint Frobenius has weights zero and one, and the middle Frobenius
is the closed densely defined maximal associated-graded source generator.

The middle carrier is definitionally `XiDivisorL2`, so this is not a source-native construction of
arithmetic cohomology.  All displayed algebraic and Hilbert identities except middle
Frobenius/Hodge commutation hold unconditionally on this comparison target.  That final
compatibility is exactly RH and is not proved here.
-/

/-- Completed degree-two Tate cohomology. -/

finite compact-support jets inside `ell^2`, inside compact-open ordinary cohomology.
-/

    DeningerArithmeticGelfandTriple DeningerArithmeticCompletedH1 :=
  deningerArithmeticJetGelfandTriple

source jet associated graded.
-/
def deningerArithmeticCompletedH1SourceEquiv :
    DeningerArithmeticCompletedH1 ≃ₗ[ℂ]
      DeningerArithmeticJetHilbert :=
  deningerArithmeticGradedHilbertEquivSourceJets

/--
Closed middle Frobenius on completed associated-graded source cohomology.

`DeningerArithmeticAssociatedGraded` proves that this diagonal operator is induced by the full
compact-open source Frobenius on every successive jet-depth quotient.
-/
def deningerArithmeticCompletedThetaH1 :
    DeningerArithmeticCompletedH1 →ₗ.[ℂ]
      DeningerArithmeticCompletedH1 :=
  deningerDivisorClosedTheta

/-- Degree-zero/degree-two Poincare cup followed by the endpoint trace. -/
def deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointCup :
    LinearMap.BilinForm ℂ ℂ :=
  LinearMap.mk₂ ℂ
    (fun a b => a * b)
    (by intros; ring)
    (by intros; simp [smul_eq_mul]; ring)
    (by intros; ring)
    (by intros; simp [smul_eq_mul]; ring)

@[simp]
theorem deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointCup_apply (a b : ℂ) :
    deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointCup a b = a * b :=
  rfl

/-- Endpoint Poincare pairing is nondegenerate. -/

    deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointHodge

    deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointCup a

  rw [deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointCup_apply,
    deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointHodge_apply,
    Complex.mul_conj]

/-- Endpoint Hodge metric is positive definite. -/

    0 < (deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointCup a
      (deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointHodge a)).re := by
  rw [deningerArithmeticCompletedEndpointCup_hodge]
  simpa using Complex.normSq_pos.mpr ha

/-- Weight-zero Frobenius on completed `H^0`. -/

    Module.End ℂ DeningerArithmeticCompletedH0 :=
  0

/-- Weight-one Frobenius on completed `H^2 = C(-1)`. -/

    Module.End ℂ DeningerArithmeticCompletedH2 :=
  LinearMap.id

@[simp]
theorem deningerArithmeticCompletedThetaH0_apply (a : ℂ) :
    deningerArithmeticCompletedThetaH0 a = 0 :=

# Actual causal evolution on the closed maximal generator graph

The input and derivative evolve together. The product Hilbert-space topology
on the closed graph supplies the complete graph norm needed for integration
of an unbounded generator, without assuming boundedness in the input norm.
-/

open Complex MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

private def graphEvolutionLinear (t : ℝ≥0) : causalGeneratorGraph →ₗ[ℂ] causalGeneratorGraph where
  toFun p := ⟨(causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.1,causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.2),by
    intro s
    change causalLowerCauchyEvolution s (causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.1)-
      causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.1 = causalOrbitIntegral s (causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.2)
    have he : causalLowerCauchyEvolution s (causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.1) =
        causalLowerCauchyEvolution t (causalLowerCauchyEvolution s p.val.1) := by
      rw [← causalLowerCauchyEvolution_add,add_comm,causalLowerCauchyEvolution_add]
    rw [he,← map_sub,p.property s,causalOrbitIntegral_commutes]⟩
  map_add' p q := by apply Subtype.ext; apply Prod.ext <;> exact map_add _ _ _
  map_smul' c p := by apply Subtype.ext; apply Prod.ext <;> exact map_smul _ _ _

/-- The literal evolution of both components of the actual maximal generator graph. -/
def causalGeneratorGraphEvolution (t : ℝ≥0) : causalGeneratorGraph →L[ℂ] causalGeneratorGraph :=
  (graphEvolutionLinear t).mkContinuous 1 (fun p => by
    change max ‖causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.1‖ ‖causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.2‖ ≤
      1 * max ‖p.val.1‖ ‖p.val.2‖
    rw [one_mul]
    exact max_le_max (causalLowerCauchyEvolution_norm_le t p.val.1)
      (causalLowerCauchyEvolution_norm_le t p.val.2))

/-- Graph evolution has the original causal orbit as its actual input component. -/
theorem causalGeneratorGraphEvolution_input (t : ℝ≥0) (p : causalGeneratorGraph) :
    causalGeneratorGraphInput (causalGeneratorGraphEvolution t p) =
      causalLowerCauchyEvolution t (causalGeneratorGraphInput p) := rfl

/-- The actual derivative output evolves by the same completed causal semigroup. -/
theorem causalGeneratorGraphEvolution_output (t : ℝ≥0) (p : causalGeneratorGraph) :
    causalGeneratorGraphOutput (causalGeneratorGraphEvolution t p) =
      causalLowerCauchyEvolution t (causalGeneratorGraphOutput p) := rfl

/-- The actual graph norm contracts under causal evolution. -/
theorem causalGeneratorGraphEvolution_norm_le (t : ℝ≥0) (p : causalGeneratorGraph) :
    ‖causalGeneratorGraphEvolution t p‖ ≤ ‖p‖ :=
  max_le_max (causalLowerCauchyEvolution_norm_le t p.val.1)
    (causalLowerCauchyEvolution_norm_le t p.val.2)

/-- The graph evolution obeys the exact additive semigroup law. -/
theorem causalGeneratorGraphEvolution_add (s t : ℝ≥0) (p : causalGeneratorGraph) :
    causalGeneratorGraphEvolution (s+t) p =
      causalGeneratorGraphEvolution s (causalGeneratorGraphEvolution t p) := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply Prod.ext <;> exact causalLowerCauchyEvolution_add _ _ _

/-- The graph semigroup starts at the identity on the actual complete graph. -/
theorem causalGeneratorGraphEvolution_zero (p : causalGeneratorGraph) :
    causalGeneratorGraphEvolution 0 p = p := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply Prod.ext <;> exact causalLowerCauchyEvolution_zero _

/-- Both graph components vary continuously, in the actual graph norm. -/
theorem causalGeneratorGraphEvolution_continuous (p : causalGeneratorGraph) :
    Continuous (fun t : ℝ≥0 => causalGeneratorGraphEvolution t p) := by
  apply continuous_induced_rng.2
  change Continuous (fun t : ℝ≥0 =>
    (causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.1,causalLowerCauchyEvolution t p.val.2))
  exact (causalLowerCauchyEvolution_continuous p.val.1).prodMk
    (causalLowerCauchyEvolution_continuous p.val.2)

/-- Away from zero, every maximal-domain orbit has its actual full real derivative. -/
theorem causalGenerator_positiveOrbit_hasDerivAt (a : ℝ) (u : causalGeneratorDomain) :
    HasDerivAt (causalForwardOrbit u.val)
      (causalForwardOrbit (causalGenerator u) (Real.exp a)) (Real.exp a) := by
  have hd := (causalOrbitPrimitive_hasDerivAt (Real.exp a) (causalGenerator u)).const_add u.val
  apply hd.congr_of_eventuallyEq
  have hpos : ∀ᶠ r : ℝ in 𝓝 (Real.exp a), 0 < r :=
    eventually_gt_nhds (Real.exp_pos a)
  filter_upwards [hpos] with r hr
  have he := (causalForwardOrbit_rightDerivative_iff _ _).1 (causalGenerator_hasRightDeriv u) r.toNNReal
  change causalForwardOrbit u.val r-u.val = causalOrbitPrimitive (r.toNNReal:ℝ) (causalGenerator u) at he
  rw [Real.coe_toNNReal r hr.le] at he
  change causalForwardOrbit u.val r = u.val+causalOrbitPrimitive r (causalGenerator u)
  rw [← he,← add_sub_assoc,add_sub_cancel_left]

end

/-- Infinite chains of genuine maximal-generator pairs, in the original countable product space. -/
def causalSmoothGraph : Submodule ℂ (ℕ → hardyL2ᗮ) :=
  ⨅ j : ℕ, causalGeneratorGraph.comap
    ((LinearMap.proj j : (ℕ → hardyL2ᗮ) →ₗ[ℂ] hardyL2ᗮ).prod (LinearMap.proj (j+1)))

theorem causalSmoothGraph_mem_iff (v : ℕ → hardyL2ᗮ) :
    v ∈ causalSmoothGraph ↔ ∀ j : ℕ, (v j, v (j+1)) ∈ causalGeneratorGraph := by
  simp only [causalSmoothGraph, Submodule.mem_iInf, Submodule.mem_comap]
  rfl

/-- The genuine infinite-chain space is closed in the product of the actual Hilbert spaces. -/
theorem isClosed_causalSmoothGraph : IsClosed (causalSmoothGraph : Set (ℕ → hardyL2ᗮ)) := by
  have he : (causalSmoothGraph : Set (ℕ → hardyL2ᗮ)) =
      {v : ℕ → hardyL2ᗮ | ∀ j : ℕ, (v j, v (j+1)) ∈ causalGeneratorGraph} :=
    Set.ext causalSmoothGraph_mem_iff
  rw [he]
  simp only [setOf_forall]
  exact isClosed_iInter (fun j => isClosed_causalGeneratorGraph.preimage
    ((continuous_apply j).prodMk (continuous_apply (j+1))))

/-- Closedness makes the actual countable chain space complete in its inherited uniformity. -/
theorem causalSmoothGraph_complete : CompleteSpace causalSmoothGraph :=
  isClosed_causalSmoothGraph.completeSpace_coe

/-- A continuous coordinate readout of a genuine infinite generator chain. -/
def causalSmoothGraphCoordinate (j : ℕ) : causalSmoothGraph →L[ℂ] hardyL2ᗮ where
  toLinearMap := (LinearMap.proj j).comp causalSmoothGraph.subtype
  cont := (continuous_apply j).comp continuous_subtype_val

/-- Every consecutive coordinate pair records the actual right derivative of its causal orbit. -/
theorem causalSmoothGraphCoordinate_hasRightDeriv (j : ℕ) (u : causalSmoothGraph) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (causalForwardOrbit (causalSmoothGraphCoordinate j u))
      (causalSmoothGraphCoordinate (j+1) u) (Ioi 0) 0 :=
  (causalGeneratorGraph_mem_iff _ _).1 ((causalSmoothGraph_mem_iff u.val).1 u.property j)

/-- Every coordinate is an element of the genuine maximal-generator domain. -/
def causalSmoothGraphDomainCoordinate (j : ℕ) (u : causalSmoothGraph) : causalGeneratorDomain :=
  ⟨causalSmoothGraphCoordinate j u, (causalGeneratorDomain_mem_iff _).2
    ⟨causalSmoothGraphCoordinate (j+1) u, causalSmoothGraphCoordinate_hasRightDeriv j u⟩⟩

/-- The actual maximal generator sends each coordinate to its literal successor. -/
theorem causalGenerator_smoothGraphCoordinate (j : ℕ) (u : causalSmoothGraph) :
    causalGenerator (causalSmoothGraphDomainCoordinate j u) = causalSmoothGraphCoordinate (j+1) u :=
  (causalGenerator_eq_iff _ _).2 (causalSmoothGraphCoordinate_hasRightDeriv j u)

/-- No two genuine infinite derivative chains have the same initial datum. -/
theorem causalSmoothGraphCoordinate_zero_injective :
    Function.Injective (causalSmoothGraphCoordinate 0) := by
  intro u v h
  apply Subtype.ext
  funext j
  induction j with
  | zero => exact h
  | succ j ih =>
    have hp : (⟨(u.val j, u.val (j+1)), (causalSmoothGraph_mem_iff u.val).1 u.property j⟩ : causalGeneratorGraph) =
        ⟨(v.val j, v.val (j+1)), (causalSmoothGraph_mem_iff v.val).1 v.property j⟩ := by
      apply causalGeneratorGraphInput_injective

    exact congrArg (fun p : causalGeneratorGraph => p.val.2) hp

theorem causalSmoothGraphCoordinate_mem_powerDomain (j k : ℕ) (u : causalSmoothGraph) :
    causalSmoothGraphCoordinate j u ∈ causalGeneratorPowerDomain k := by

/-!
# Contact-free nonlinear Teukolsky causal cut

Compare the complete retarded and advanced `++-` Schur sources while keeping the same local
Einstein Taylor data. Their difference kills the direct third derivative before any cokernel
projection. The surviving nonlinear causal cut is exactly the bilinear Einstein coupling applied
to the `++` and `+-` response-map jumps.

Consequently, no coherent same-grade local third-order counterterm can alter this cut. A nonzero
cut must be carried by a discontinuity of at least one complete bulk-plus-horizon response.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

variable {X Y : Type*}
  [AddCommGroup X] [Module ℂ X]
  [AddCommGroup Y] [Module ℂ Y]

/-- Retarded-minus-advanced cut of the complete nonlinear `++-` Schur source. -/
def d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (C : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X) : Y :=
  d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusSchurSource
      B C RppRet RpmRet p m -
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusSchurSource
      B C RppAdv RpmAdv p m

/-- The total causal cut contains response discontinuities and no direct third-order residual. -/
theorem d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_responseDifference
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (C : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X) :
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut
        B C RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m =
      B p (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyRetardedPlusMinusResponse B RpmRet p m -
        d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyRetardedPlusMinusResponse B RpmAdv p m) +
      B m (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyRetardedPlusPlusResponse B RppRet p -
        d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyRetardedPlusPlusResponse B RppAdv p) := by
  simp [d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut,
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusSchurSource, map_sub]
  abel

/-- Resolvent-jump form of the contact-free nonlinear causal cut. -/
theorem d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_resolventJump
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (C : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X) :
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut
        B C RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m =
      B p ((RpmRet - RpmAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusMinusResidual B p m)) +
      B m ((RppRet - RppAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p)) := by
  rw [d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_responseDifference]
  simp [d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyRetardedPlusMinusResponse,
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyRetardedPlusPlusResponse]

/-- No change of the common direct Einstein third jet changes the nonlinear causal cut. -/
theorem d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_independent_directThirdJet
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (C₁ C₂ : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X) :
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut
        B C₁ RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m =
      d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut
        B C₂ RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m := by
  rw [d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_resolventJump,
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_resolventJump]

/-- If both sourced response discontinuities vanish, the total nonlinear causal cut vanishes. -/
theorem d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_zero_of_responseJumps_eq_zero
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (C : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X)
    (hpm : (RpmRet - RpmAdv)
      (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusMinusResidual B p m) = 0)
    (hpp : (RppRet - RppAdv)
      (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p) = 0) :
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut
        B C RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m = 0 := by
  rw [d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_resolventJump,
    hpm, hpp]
  simp

/-- Nonzero total causal source localizes to a nonzero sourced `+-` or `++` response jump. -/
theorem d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_ne_zero_imp_responseJump
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (C : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X)
    (hcut : d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut
      B C RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m ≠ 0) :
    (RpmRet - RpmAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusMinusResidual B p m) ≠ 0 ∨
      (RppRet - RppAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p) ≠ 0 := by
  contrapose! hcut
  exact d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCausalCut_eq_zero_of_responseJumps_eq_zero
    B C RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m hcut.1 hcut.2
